questions.question:
Convert the assertive sentence into Indirect Speech:
Ramesh said, "I work in the High Court registry."

options.text: Ramesh said that he worked in the High Court registry.
Ramesh told that he worked in the High Court registry.
Ramesh said that I worked in the High Court registry.
Ramesh said that he has worked in the High Court registry.

questions.explanation: Direct sentence mein reporting verb 'said' past tense mein hai aur listener specify nahi hai, isliye 'said that' aayega. 1st person pronoun 'I' speaker Ramesh (male singular) ke anusaar 'he' banega, aur Simple Present verb 'work' backshift hokar Simple Past 'worked' banegi. Option (A) bilkul accurate hai. Option (B) mein 'told' bina object ke use kiya gaya hai jo non-standard hai. Option (C) mein pronoun 'I' ko change nahi kiya gaya. Option (D) mein tense ko backshift nahi kiya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01 & RC-06: Assertive Conversion & Simple Present to Simple Past backshift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The registrar said to me, "You are eligible for the technical assistant post."

options.text: The registrar told to me that I was eligible for the technical assistant post.
The registrar told me that I was eligible for the technical assistant post.
The registrar said me that I was eligible for the technical assistant post.
The registrar told me that you were eligible for the technical assistant post.

questions.explanation: Direct speech mein 'said to me' aane par reporting verb 'told me' mein convert hoti hai (bina preposition 'to' ke). 2nd person pronoun 'You' listener 'me' ke anusaar 'I' banega, aur present tense 'are' backshift hokar 'was' banega. Option (B) bilkul correct hai. Option (A) mein fatal 'told to me' blunder hai. Option (C) mein 'said me' galat construction hai. Option (D) mein 2nd person pronoun 'you' ko change nahi kiya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02 & RC-04: Said to ➔ Told + Object & 2nd Person Pronoun Shift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Present Continuous Backshift & Time Expression Shift
questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
Pooja said, "I am drafting the official compliance report now."

options.text: Pooja said that she was drafting the official compliance report then.
Pooja said that she is drafting the official compliance report then.
Pooja said that she had drafted the official compliance report now.
Pooja said that she was drafting the official compliance report now.

questions.explanation: Reporting verb 'said' past tense mein hai. 1st person 'I' Pooja ke anusaar 'she' banega. Present Continuous 'am drafting' backshift hokar Past Continuous 'was drafting' banega. Time adverbial 'now' shift hokar 'then' banega. Option (A) dono rules ko flawlessly apply karta hai. Option (B) mein tense backshift nahi kiya gaya. Option (C) mein continuous ko perfect bana diya gaya aur 'now' ko retain rakha. Option (D) mein 'now' ko 'then' mein badla nahi gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06 & RC-10: Present Continuous ➔ Past Continuous & Now ➔ Then.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Present Perfect Backshift & Plural Pronoun Shift
questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The system engineers said, "We have completed the data migration."

options.text: The system engineers said that they have completed the data migration.
The system engineers said that we had completed the data migration.
The system engineers said that they had completed the data migration.
The system engineers told that they completed the data migration.

questions.explanation: Reporting subject 'The system engineers' plural hai, isliye 1st person plural pronoun 'We' badal kar 'they' banega. Reporting verb past mein hone ke karan Present Perfect 'have completed' backshift hokar Past Perfect 'had completed' banega. Option (C) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) mein tense backshift missing hai. Option (B) mein 'we' ko 'they' mein nahi badla gaya. Option (D) mein 'told' bina object ke hai aur Past Perfect ke bajaye Simple Past use kiya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03 & RC-06: 1st Person Plural Shift & Present Perfect ➔ Past Perfect.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Simple Past to Past Perfect Shift & Yesterday Adjustment
questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The clerk said, "The advocate filed the writ petition yesterday."

options.text: The clerk said that the advocate filed the writ petition the previous day.
The clerk said that the advocate had filed the writ petition the previous day.
The clerk said that the advocate has filed the writ petition yesterday.
The clerk told that the advocate had filed the writ petition yesterday.

questions.explanation: Direct speech mein Simple Past 'filed' aaya hai. Past reporting verb ke sath Simple Past compulsory Past Perfect ('had filed') mein backshift hota hai. Time expression 'yesterday' shift hokar 'the previous day' (ya 'the day before') banega. Option (B) dono adjustments accurate execute karta hai. Option (A) mein Simple Past ko Past Perfect mein backshift nahi kiya gaya (classic exam pitfall). Option (C) mein Present Perfect bana diya gaya. Option (D) mein 'yesterday' ko unadjusted chhod diya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07 & RC-10: Simple Past ➔ Past Perfect & Yesterday ➔ The previous day.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Past Continuous to Past Perfect Continuous Shift
questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
Kavita said, "The bench was hearing urgent appeals in Courtroom 3."

options.text: Kavita said that the bench was hearing urgent appeals in Courtroom 3.
Kavita said that the bench had heard urgent appeals in Courtroom 3.
Kavita said that the bench had been hearing urgent appeals in Courtroom 3.
Kavita told that the bench has been hearing urgent appeals in Courtroom 3.

questions.explanation: Direct speech mein Past Continuous 'was hearing' use hua hai. Past reporting verb 'said' ke under Past Continuous hamesha Past Perfect Continuous ('had been hearing') mein backshift hota hai. Option (C) bilkul correct hai. Option (A) mein tense backshift nahi kiya gaya. Option (B) mein continuous aspect ko drop karke Past Perfect simple bana diya gaya. Option (D) mein Present Perfect Continuous lagaya gaya jo invalid hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Past Continuous ➔ Past Perfect Continuous (was/were + V4 ➔ had been + V4).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The judicial officer said, "The committee will inspect the server room tomorrow."

options.text: The judicial officer said that the committee would inspect the server room the next day.
The judicial officer said that the committee will inspect the server room tomorrow.
The judicial officer said that the committee should inspect the server room the next day.
The judicial officer told that the committee would inspect the server room tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Reporting verb 'said' past tense mein hai. Future modal auxiliary 'will' backshift hokar 'would' banegi. Time adverbial 'tomorrow' shift hokar 'the next day' (ya 'the following day') banega. Option (A) dono transformations flawlessly execute karta hai. Option (B) mein na toh modal backshift hua aur na hi time expression. Option (C) mein 'will' ko 'should' (obligation) bana kar meaning distort kar diya gaya. Option (D) mein 'tomorrow' ko unadjusted chhod diya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08 & RC-10: Will ➔ Would & Tomorrow ➔ The next day.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
Manish said to Suresh, "I cannot verify this digital certificate."

options.text: Manish told to Suresh that he could not verify that digital certificate.
Manish told Suresh that he could not verify that digital certificate.
Manish told Suresh that he cannot verify this digital certificate.
Manish said Suresh that he could not verify that digital certificate.

questions.explanation: 'Said to Suresh' ➔ 'told Suresh' (bina 'to' ke). 1st person 'I' Manish ke anusaar 'he' banega. Modal 'cannot' ➔ 'could not' mein backshift hoga. Demonstrative adjective 'this' ➔ 'that' mein shift hoga. Option (B) sabhi rules ko perfectly satisfy karta hai. Option (A) mein fatal 'told to' blunder hai. Option (C) mein tense aur demonstrative shifts missing hain. Option (D) mein 'said Suresh' invalid syntax hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02, RC-08 & RC-10: Said to ➔ Told, Can ➔ Could & This ➔ That.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Scientific Fact Exception to Tense Backshift
questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The science teacher said, "Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius."

options.text: The science teacher said that water boiled at 100 degrees Celsius.
The science teacher said that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
The science teacher told that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
The science teacher said that water had boiled at 100 degrees Celsius.

questions.explanation: Quoted sentence 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius' ek established scientific fact hai. Narration ka universal rule hai ki scientific laws aur eternal truths past reporting verb ke bawajood Simple Present tense mein hi rehte hain (zero backshift). Option (B) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) mein 'boiled' likhne ka matlab nikalta hai ki water ab 100°C par boil nahi hota, jo absurd hai. Option (C) mein 'told' bina object ke hai. Option (D) mein Past Perfect use kiya gaya jo invalid hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Universal Truths & Scientific Laws Exception (No Backshift).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The IT head says, "The main judicial database is running smoothly."

options.text: The IT head says that the main judicial database was running smoothly.
The IT head said that the main judicial database was running smoothly.
The IT head says that the main judicial database is running smoothly.
The IT head says that the main judicial database had been running smoothly.

questions.explanation: Reporting verb 'says' Simple Present Tense mein hai. Narration ka fundamental rule hai ki jab reporting verb Present ya Future tense mein ho, toh reported speech ke tense mein koi backshift NAHI hota! Verb 'is running' uninflected Present Continuous mein retain rahegi. Option (C) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein galat tareeqe se tense backshift kiya gaya. Option (B) mein reporting verb ko hi past bana diya gaya. Option (D) mein Past Perfect Continuous bana diya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Present Reporting Verb (Says) ➔ Zero Tense Backshift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
Rajesh said to me, "He has submitted his resignation."

options.text: Rajesh told me that I had submitted my resignation.
Rajesh told me that he had submitted his resignation.
Rajesh told to me that he has submitted his resignation.
Rajesh said to me that he has submitted his resignation.

questions.explanation: 'Said to me' ➔ 'told me'. Quoted sentence mein pronouns 'He' aur 'his' 3rd person hain. 3rd person pronouns mein koi person change nahi hota (SON rule: N = No Change), isliye 'he' aur 'his' retain rahenge. Present Perfect 'has submitted' past reporting verb ke karan Past Perfect 'had submitted' mein backshift hoga. Option (B) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) mein 3rd person ko 1st person mein badal kar meaning distort kar diya gaya. Option (C) mein 'told to me' blunder hai aur tense backshift nahi hua.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05 & RC-06: 3rd Person Pronoun Invariance & Present Perfect ➔ Past Perfect.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Error Spotting in Indirect Speech Construction
questions.question: Identify the grammatically incorrect indirect speech sentence:

options.text: The advocate told the magistrate that the witness had arrived.
The superintendent told to the clerk that the order had been signed.
The clerk said that the cause list had been updated on the website.
The judge remarked that the legal argument was compelling.

questions.explanation: Sentence (B) grammatically incorrect hai kyunki yahan 'told to the clerk' likha hai. 'Tell' ek transitive verb hai jiske baad preposition 'to' lagana strictly forbidden hota hai; correct construction 'told the clerk' hona chahiye. Sentences (A), (C), aur (D) bilkul sahi hain: (A) mein 'told the magistrate' transitive direct object hai, (C) mein 'said that' bina object ke hai, aur (D) mein 'remarked that' appropriate reporting verb hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02 & Pitfall PIT-01: 'Told to + Object' Prepositional Blunder.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06
